source_implies_lean.reasoning: Any source-compliant interface solver/flux uses Q_(i-1) and Q_i in this order, so its piecewise input and resulting binary interface-flux application satisfy the Lean facts.

findings.source_evidence: The source uses Q_(i-1),Q_i as Riemann states, solves exactly or approximately for wave information, computes an approximating interface flux, and uses it in the cell-average update.
findings.lean_evidence: riemannInterfaceFlux merely applies an unrestricted binary function to the two states; no solver, consistency, approximation, or update property occurs.
findings.impact: Correct state ordering alone is insufficient, so Lean is a materially weaker claim.

rationale: A source-compliant exact or approximate Riemann-flux construction uses the same ordered neighboring states and therefore satisfies the Lean data/equality facts. Lean does not imply the source because riemannFlux is entirely arbitrary: there is no Riemann solve, wave information, physical-flux approximation/consistency condition, or use of the result in a cell-average time update.
